conbody.p: A project can have a cover photo, shown across the top of its Overview and beside the project in All projects. Before there is one, a slim box at the top of the page offers Add a cover photo; choose a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image. A large photo is scaled down in your browser before it is saved, and a file over 5 MB is refused. Once there is a cover, it runs across the whole page, with the project's four figures (traced, verified, failing and suspect) along its foot, so the panels beside the definition start higher up. Change cover in the photo's top corner replaces it and Remove takes it away; the figures then go back to the top of their column. Anyone who can see the project sees its cover; changing it takes an editor.

You can also have a cover made for you. Ask the V&V Assistant for one ("draw a cover for this project") and it draws a picture of the product or its setting into a Cover photo card, which shows the picture; Set as cover sets it. The assistant draws it itself, on your own runner, so there is no image service to set up and nothing extra to pay. Ask again for a different picture, or ask it to remove the cover. Agents, and AI apps you connect to the workspace, can draw, set or remove a cover with their OpenV tools in the same way.

A drawn cover is an illustration. For a photo-like picture, a workspace admin can add the workspace's OpenAI API key under Workspace settings, AI providers; the assistant then offers a photo card when you ask for a photo, made by OpenAI's image model and paid for with that key. A workspace can generate a limited number of photos an hour.
